ImageDescription.value: Alonso Vázquez pinta, óleo sobre lienzo, el Tránsito de San Hermenegildo (492 X 340 cm), para el retablo mayor de la iglesia del Hospital de San Hermenegildo o del Cardenal, conocido popularmente como de los heridos, fundado por el Cardenal Cervantes (1455). Como era habitual en esas fechas, su composición, dividida en dos, la superior la espiritual y la inferior la terrenal. Por ausencia del autor, Juan de Uceda termina la obra (1603-1604) con algunas figuras de los ángeles, parte superior. El ático del retablo de Diego López Bueno (1603) de encuentra en Iglesia de San Román, Sevilla.

ImageDescription.value: “It is a 14th-century Mudéjar church, although it was renovated in the Baroque style in the 18th century. In 1936, during the Spanish Civil War, it suffered a fire that destroyed its entire interior. It has since been restored several times, most recently in 2004. … The Baroque bell tower, dating from 1700, has two sections, the second decorated with Solomonic columns. It is topped by a striking capital covered in blue tiles.” Source: @visitarsevillacom (Google-translated)
